heading: What is Git and why do we use it?
content:
Git is a distributed version control system that tracks every change
made to code over time and lets multiple developers work on the same
project without overwriting each other's work.

heading: Explain about the Git vs GitHub?
content:
•Git = CLI-based, local tool on your machine

•GitHub = UI-based, cloud platform that hosts Git repositories so the
team can collaborate remotely

We work locally with Git (add, commit), then push to GitHub, or
pull/clone from GitHub.

heading: Why Git matters in my banking project?
content:
Our development team uses Git to manage the code for modules like
Accounts, Cards, Loans, and Payments. If a deployment causes a
production issue, Git lets the team quickly identify the problematic
change and revert to a previous stable version --- critical in a banking
environment where downtime directly affects customers.

As a Production Support Engineer, I use Git to check what recently
changed during an incident (git log, git diff) and to speak the same
language as developers during release and Change Management discussions.

heading: Commands --- Setup
parentHeading: Why Git matters in my banking project?
content:
• git --version --- check installed version

• git config --global user.name "Afsa" / user.email --- sets identity
for commits

• git config --list --- verify configuration(you make is tagged with
your name and email --- similar to how every ticket in ServiceNow is
tagged with the engineer who worked on it.)

heading: Commands --- Tracking changes
parentHeading: Why Git matters in my banking project?
content:
• git init --- starts version tracking in a folder (Initializes a new,
empty Git repository in a folder. for example, if the development team
starts a brand-new module for our banking app)

• git add filename.txt / git add . --- stages changes for commit

• git commit -m "message" --- saves staged changes with a description
(e.g., "Fixed OTP delivery delay")

• git status --- shows current state: changed, staged, untracked files

• git diff --- shows exact line-by-line changes vs. last commit

• git log / git log --oneline --- shows commit history --- useful to
check what changed after a release. (Shows the full history of commits
--- who changed what and when. If there's a production issue after a
release)

heading: Commands --- Branching
parentHeading: Why Git matters in my banking project?
content:
• git branch icici-loan / git branch --- creates/lists branches (e.g.,
separate branch for Loans feature)

• git switch icici-loan --- switches to that branch(e.g another module
created In bank application)

• git merge icici-loan --- merges tested changes back into main branch
--- same idea as going live in production

heading: Commands --- GitHub (remote)
parentHeading: Why Git matters in my banking project?
content:
• git clone \<url\> --- downloads an existing
repository(Downloads/copies an entire existing repository from GitHub
onto your local machine.)

• git push origin main --- uploads local commits to GitHub

• git pull origin main --- downloads latest changes from GitHub

heading: Example of an issue you faced involving Git?
content:
Yes --- there was an incident where customers started reporting that the
loan payoff amount shown on the dashboard was incorrect, right after a
release had gone out that morning.

Since this happened soon after a deployment, my first step was to check
with the development team what had changed. I asked them to show me the
git log for that release, so we could see the recent commits made to the
Loans module.

This helped us confirm that a change had indeed gone in the previous day
related to loan interest calculation logic.
